⇒ x/100 ≈ 0.055

**Therefore, the rate of interest per annum compounded annually is 5.5%.**

questions.question: A manufacturer earns a profit of 10% on selling his products to a wholesale dealer. The wholesale dealer earns a profit of 15% by selling it to a retailer. The retailer, in turn, earns a profit of 25% from the customer. What is the actual cost of production of an article for which the customer pays Rs. 12,650?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Customer pays = Rs. 12,650.

Profit to retailer = 25%.

Profit to wholesale dealer = 15%.

Profit to manufacturer = 10%.

**Formula Used:**

Actual cost = Final amount / [(1 + Profit percentage/100)ⁿ], where n is the number of times the profit is applied.

**Calculation:**

Let the cost of production be Rs. x.

⇒ Price after manufacturer's profit = x × (1 + 10/100)

⇒ Price after wholesale dealer's profit = x × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 15/100)

⇒ Price after retailer's profit = x × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 15/100) × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ 12,650 = x × (1.1) × (1.15) × (1.25)

⇒ 12,650 = x × 1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25

⇒ x = 12,650 / (1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25)

⇒ x = 12,650 / 1.58125

⇒ x = 8,000

**The actual cost of production of the article is Rs. 8,000.**

questions.question: By selling a TV set for Rs. 16,800, a salesman gains a profit of 20%. If the production cost is increased by 20%, find the new selling price of the set so as to gain 20%.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Original selling price of the TV set = Rs. 16,800

Profit gained = 20%

Production cost increase = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price × 100

New Cost Price = Original Cost Price × (1 + Percentage Increase)

New Selling Price = New Cost Price × (1 + Desired Profit Percentage)

**Calculation:**

Let the original cost price be CP.

⇒ 20% of CP = 16800 - CP

⇒ 0.20 × CP = 16800 - CP

⇒ 1.20 × CP = 16800

⇒ CP = 16800 / 1.20

⇒ CP = 14000

With a 20% increase in production cost,

New CP = 14000 × (1 + 20/100)

New CP = 14000 × 1.20

New CP = 16800

To gain a 20% profit on the new CP,

New SP = 16800 × (1 + 20/100)

New SP = 16800 × 1.20

New SP = 20160

**The new selling price of the TV set to gain a 20% profit is Rs. 20,160.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of milk to water in a mixture is 9 ∶ 7.

The mixture contains 4 litres more milk than water.

**Formula Used:**

If the ratio of milk to water is 9 ∶ 7, then let the quantity of milk be 9x litres and the quantity of water be 7x litres.

**Calculation:**

Quantity of milk = Quantity of water + 4 litres

⇒ 9x = 7x + 4

⇒ 9x - 7x = 4

⇒ 2x = 4

⇒ x = 2

Quantity of milk = 9x = 9 × 2 = 18 litres

**The quantity of milk in the mixture is 18 litres.**

questions.question: Juli and Rahul can simultaneously finish the work of painting a room in 12 days. If Juli alone can paint the room in 20 days, in how many days can Rahul alone complete the same work of painting the room?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Juli and Rahul together can finish painting the room in 12 days.

Juli alone can paint the room in 20 days.

**Formula used:**

Work done by Juli in one day = 1/20

Work done by Juli and Rahul together in one day = 1/12

Work done by Rahul in one day = Work done by Juli and Rahul together in one day - Work done by Juli in one day

Time taken by Rahul alone to complete the work = 1 / Work done by Rahul in one day

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by Juli in one day = 1/20

⇒ Work done by Juli and Rahul together in one day = 1/12

⇒ Work done by Rahul in one day = 1/12 - 1/20

⇒ Work done by Rahul in one day = (5 - 3) / 60

⇒ Work done by Rahul in one day = 2 / 60

⇒ Work done by Rahul in one day = 1 / 30

⇒ Time taken by Rahul alone to complete the work = 30 days

**∴ Rahul alone can complete the work in 30 days.**

Mean proportion of a and b = √(a×b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ (3 + 2√2)² = 9 + 12√2 + 8 = 17 + 12√2

⇒ (3 - 2√2)² = 9 - 12√2 + 8 = 17 - 12√2

Now, find the mean proportion.

⇒ Mean proportion = √[(17 + 12√2)×(17 - 12√2)]

⇒ Mean proportion = √[(17)² - (12√2)²]

⇒ Mean proportion = √[289 - 288]

⇒ Mean proportion = √1

⇒ Mean proportion = 1

**The mean proportion of (3 + 2√2)² and (3 - 2√2)² is 1.**

questions.question: A work can be completed by P and Q working separately in 12 and 18 days, respectively. But they work on alternate days beginning with P. How many days will it take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.

Efficiency: P = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day, Q = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day.

Work done in 2 days (P then Q) = 3 + 2 = 5 units.

In 14 days (7 cycles), work done = 5 × 7 = 35 units.

Remaining 1 unit is completed by P in 1/3 day. Total time = 14 + 1/3 = 14¹/₃ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14¹/₃ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P alone = 12 days

Time taken by Q alone = 18 days

They work on alternate days starting with P.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days Taken

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P
 12
 36
 3
 
 

 Q
 18
 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in the first 2 days (1 cycle) = 3 (by P) + 2 (by Q) = 5 units.

⇒ Number of complete cycles possible for 36 units = 36 ÷ 5 = 7 cycles (which covers 35 units of work).

⇒ Time taken for 7 cycles = 7 × 2 = 14 days.

⇒ Remaining work = 36 − 35 = 1 unit.

⇒ On the 15th day, it is P's turn. Time taken to complete the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of P = 1/3 day.

⇒ Total time taken = 14 days + 1/3 day = 14¹/₃ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14¹/₃ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Days Concept

When individuals work on alternate days, the work pattern repeats in cycles. Always calculate the work done in one complete cycle and multiply it by the largest possible integer without exceeding the total work, then assign the remaining work to the person whose turn is next.

Pipes & Cisterns

This topic follows the exact same efficiency concepts as Time and Work. Inlets act as positive work, while outlets or leaks act as negative work, meaning their efficiency is subtracted from the total combined efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work completed by each individual. If workers work together for the entire duration, wages are divided directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: Two trains of length 200 m and 325 m long are running on parallel rail tracks at speeds of 78 km/h and 60 km/h. respectively. In how much time (in seconds) the faster train cross the slower one if they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the first train = 200 m.

Length of the second train = 325 m.

Speed of the first train = 78 km/h.

Speed of the second train = 60 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed when two objects are moving in the same direction = Speed of faster object - Speed of slower object.

Time = Distance / Speed.

**Calculation:**

Total length to be crossed = Length of the first train + Length of the second train = 200 + 325 = 525 m.

Convert speeds from km/h to m/s by multiplying with (5)/(18) .

Speed of the first train in m/s = 78 × (5)/(18) = 21.67 m/s.

Speed of the second train in m/s = 60 × (5)/(18) = 16.67 m/s.

Relative speed = 21.67 - 16.67 = 5 m/s.

Time taken to cross = Total distance / Relative speed = 525 / 5 = 105 seconds.

**The time taken for the faster train to cross the slower one is 105 seconds.**

questions.question: A college student spends 75% of his pocket money. When the pocket money increased by 20%, the expenditure also increased by 15%. What is the increase in the savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Expenditure** to **Savings** = 75 : 25 = 3 : 1.

Using the weighted average method: **Income Increase** = (Exp × Exp% + Sav × Sav%) ÷ Total Ratio.

20% = (3 × 15% + 1 × x%) ÷ 4.

80 = 45 + x ⇒ x = 35%.

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Pocket Money** (Income) = 100 units

Initial **Expenditure** = 75% of 100 = 75 units

Initial **Savings** = 100 − 75 = 25 units

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/827ddea52434b1e942f8faf138dbad8e6219927a8facb4922167fc8162a1d9cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ New **Pocket Money** = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120 units

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 75 + 15% of 75 = 75 + 11.25 = 86.25 units

⇒ New **Savings** = New Income − New Expenditure = 120 − 86.25 = 33.75 units

⇒ Increase in **Savings** = 33.75 − 25 = 8.75 units

⇒ Percentage Increase in **Savings** = (8.75 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 0.35 × 100 = 35%

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings Relationship

The basic equation is **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. Any change in two variables directly impacts the third.

Weighted Average (Alligation Method)

Percentage change in **Income** is the weighted average of percentage changes in **Expenditure** and **Savings**: %ΔI = (E × %ΔE + S × %ΔS) ÷ (E + S).

Percentage Change Formula

To find the percentage increase or decrease, use: **[(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100**.</p

questions.question: Among the given options, which one causes an echo?

__
 
• **Echo** is a phenomenon where sound waves are reflected back to the listener, causing a repetition of the original sound.
 
• For an echo to be heard, the reflected sound must reach the listener at least 0.1 seconds after the original sound.
 
• The distance between the sound source and the reflecting surface must be significant for an echo to be perceived.
 
• Common environments where echoes are noticed include large empty halls, mountains, and canyons.

• **Sound Reflection**: The bouncing back of sound waves when they hit a surface that does not absorb the sound.
 
• **Absorption**: Some materials absorb sound waves, preventing echoes. Examples include carpets and curtains.
 
• **Reverberation**: Unlike an echo, reverberation is the persistence of sound in a particular space after the original sound is produced.
 
• **Acoustic Design**: Modern architecture often incorporates materials and designs to manage echoes and reverberation in buildings.
